attrs.evidence: INV-R8.2 made promotion final and published across two separate git ref transactions — compare-and-swap the canonical branch, then `git tag` the revision id. GPT-5.6 reproduced the split: with the tag absent at the check, the CAS succeeds, an interleaved writer creates the revision id against another commit, and `git tag` then fails, leaving the canonical branch at the candidate while the revision identity names a stranger. A crash between the two commands leaves the analogous canonical-but-untagged state. Either way the successor is VISIBLE TO EVERY READER before its identity exists, and the refusal fires after the thing it refuses has happened — which is the defect INV-R8.2 corrected one layer up and reintroduced one layer down. Repair: `git update-ref --stdin` in start/prepare/commit form carries `update <ref> <new> <expected-old>` and `create refs/tags/<id> <new>` in a single transaction; git locks every ref at prepare and moves none unless all locks hold. Reproduced in both directions before and after (scripts/factory-station.mjs selftest, MUT-PUBLICATION-TAG-RACE and MUT-PUBLICATION-HEAD-RACE), each paired with the SUPERSEDED two-step sequence on identical inputs as a differential control.
attrs.gap: ATOMIC WITHIN ONE REPOSITORY, WHICH IS THE ONLY PLACE THE CANONICAL STATE LIVES — but git ref transactions are atomic per repository, so a future factory whose canonical state spanned two repositories, or a repository plus an index, would need a protocol this claim does not supply. Second, and unchanged from FAC-CANONICAL-HEAD-CAS: this binds a session that CALLS the station. It cannot bind one that writes the shared directory and never promotes. Third: `create` refuses a revision id that exists, so the id space is the boundary of identity here — two factories sharing a repository and a naming scheme would collide correctly, two using different schemes would not collide at all.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/factory-station.mjs — publish() and the promote path; the differential control is in selftest
attrs.prior_art: git-update-ref(1), transactional mode: refs are locked at `prepare` with their expected values and the transaction aborts rather than partially committing. GPT-5.6 named the primitive in its audit of INV-R8.2. The property is the one SLSA Source v1.2 assumes when it treats a revision as a logically immutable snapshot — a snapshot whose identity is assigned after publication was, for a window, a different object under the same name.
attrs.review_focus: The claim is about a COMPOSITION, not a primitive. INV-R8.2's selftest proved `git update-ref` compares before it swaps and `git tag` refuses to move an existing tag — both true, both still true, and neither able to observe this defect, because the defect was in the order `promote` called them. Is `publish()` now the only path by which either ref moves, and is the differential control the right shape for a repair — running the superseded implementation on identical inputs and asserting it produces the split state?
attrs.statement: Publishing a canonical successor and establishing its immutable revision identity is ONE all-or-none factory operation: either the canonical ref advances AND the revision id is created for that exact commit, or neither ref moves.
